alert.note: the ALERT LIMIT setup() arms with a pin wired (max_current_ma 5000), read from the transcript; null for poll only. A trip of 0 mA arms a limit of 0, as plan B writes it

calibration.note: the CALIBRATION value setup() writes; null where plan B setup fails before writing it

cases.name: present
cases.output: id 0x22 ok -- device present; setup failed AFTER detect (init / config / timing)

cases.name: unpowered
cases.output: id reads 0x00 -- chip-select not asserting, or device unpowered

cases.name: idle_high
cases.output: id reads 0xFF -- bus idle-high: no device driving MISO (absent / MISO miswired)

cases.name: crosswired
cases.output: id reads 0x40, expected 0x22 -- wrong device on this bus/select (crosswired)

cases.name: absent
cases.output: no bus response -- device not acking (absent / unpowered / miswired)

diagnose.note: diagnose(): one byte of the die id; the verdict text

probe.note: probe(): the transcript and the step that failed ('die id', 'read'), null when it passed

read.note: _read() with _max_current_ma: the transcript (three 2-byte reads: 0x02, 0x04, 0x03) and the mV / mA / mW

divergence.note: the port also restores ALERT LIMIT and MASK/ENABLE, which the general call cleared and plan B left so: the same two writes setup made, after plan B two; a refused one ends the re-arm and fails it

rearm.note: rearm() after a healthy setup (its transcript in `setup`): the re-arm transcript and ok (plan B logs a failure); a case with a divergence owes its script and ok instead -- an armed alert, whose two extra writes plan B never made, so a refusal of either fails only the port

setup.note: setup() over a scripted part: input the component block, whether an alert pin is wired and the transcript; output ok, the CALIBRATION written (null on failure) and the alert trip armed (0: none, or poll only)
